newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares finish lower in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares finish lower in volatile trade.

text.p: Bombay shares finished lower on Tuesday in volatile trade driven by punters, traders said.
They said funds were cautious participants.
"Funds were semi-active. Most of the action was driven by speculators," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index swung wildly hitting a mid-session high of 3035.64 points. It closed a provisional 44.4 points down at the day's low of 2950.58 points.
Technical analyst Mehmood Khan at Times Guaranty Financial Ltd said the index was likely to form a new bottom at 2905-2865 levels.
"For the current week, the BSE index may find support at 2905, 2878 and 2858 points. On the higher end it may encounter resistance at 3054-3125 levels," Khan said.
First half company results -- for the period ended September 30, 1996 -- continued to drive prices.

ITC shares traded between a low of 273.50 rupees and a high of 289.25 rupees as punters squared positions after the firm's first half results beat market expectations. The firm said on Monday net profit rose to 1.81 billion rupees in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) from 1.41 billion a year ago.
Forecasts had ranged from 1.5 billion to 1.7 billion rupees.
ITC ended 0.25 rupees lower on the BSE at 275.50 and 0.55 rupees higher on the NSE at 278.05.
Shares of GE Shipping fell 0.75 rupees to 29.25 after the firm said its first half net fell below the year-ago.
Shares of Indian Hotels fell 10 rupees to 646 though its first half net at 513.2 million rupees against 442.6 million met most market expectations.
Prices on the NSE shot past BSE levels on hectic squaring off on the last day of the account.
Auto firms TELCO, Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra continued to head lower as some securities firms recommended investors underweight the sector on fears of a prolonged slowdown in the economy.
